title: Decorate a name like MSVC
description:
Write the decorator from the lesson for free functions with simple types:

```cpp
std::string decorate(const std::string& name, const std::string& returnType, const std::vector<std::string>& parameters);
```

The result is `?` + name + `@@YA` + the return type's code + the parameter codes + an ending:

- with at least one parameter, the ending is `@Z`;
- with no parameters, the parameter list is `X` (void) and the ending is `Z`, so the name ends in `XZ`.

| Type | Code | Type | Code |
|---|---|---|---|
| `void` | `X` | `int` | `H` |
| `char` | `D` | `unsigned int` | `I` |
| `bool` | `_N` | `long long` | `_J` |
| `float` | `M` | `double` | `N` |

If any type is not in the table, return an empty string.

```
decorate("add", "int", { "int", "int" })     == "?add@@YAHHH@Z"
decorate("reset", "void", {})                == "?reset@@YAXXZ"
decorate("ratio", "double", { "float", "bool" }) == "?ratio@@YANM_N@Z"
```
hints: Keep the table in a `std::map<std::string, std::string>`. Check the return type first, then build the parameter part.
